**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** October 18, 2026
**Re:** Harrowgate Provisions, Inc. / Tessaline Polymers LLC supply documents: issues for the Corvane Equity Partners IV, L.P. transaction

**Privileged & Confidential | Attorney Work Product**

---

## I. Executive Summary

I reviewed the three Tessaline supply documents together:

- the Master Supply Agreement (MSA);
- Order Form No. 1 (Order Form);
- the Quality Agreement.

All three are dated March 1, 2026 (the Effective Date) and are governed by Delaware law (MSA §17.1). Under MSA §1.3, the Order Form controls in a conflict, then the MSA, then the Quality Agreement.

I found **four issues**, ranked by significance below.

| Rank | Issue | Location | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Change-of-control consent triggered by the Corvane merger | MSA §15.3 (with §1.1(c), §15.2; Order Form §2.1) | **Immediate attention.** Address before the merger agreement is signed. |
| 2 | Harrowgate's indemnity is uncapped; Tessaline's is capped | MSA §11.4 (with §§10.1, 10.2, 11.1, 11.2) | High. This is a diligence point for Corvane. Raise it in the same Tessaline negotiation as Issue 1. |
| 3 | Automatic five-year renewals with a narrow 30-day opt-out window | Order Form §2.2 (with §§2.1, 3.1) | Medium. Fix it now while we have leverage, and docket the window. |
| 4 | Tessaline may assign freely; Harrowgate may not | MSA §15.1 (compare §15.2) | Medium. Include it in the same amendment. |

**Quality Agreement.** I found no issue requiring renegotiation. Its terms are customary or favorable to Harrowgate. See Part IV.

**Bottom line.** The Corvane merger will trigger Tessaline's consent right under MSA §15.3. If closing occurs without consent, Tessaline may terminate and accelerate the unpaid minimum purchase commitment for the rest of the term. We should obtain a written consent and waiver before signing. I recommend using that one approach to Tessaline to also fix Issues 2 through 4 through a single amendment.

---

## II. Key Commercial Terms (for context)

- **Effective Date:** March 1, 2026 (MSA Preamble; Order Form Preamble).
- **Initial Term:** three years from the Effective Date (Order Form §2.1). This runs to approximately March 1, 2029.
- **Renewal:** automatic, for successive five-year Renewal Terms (Order Form §2.2).
- **Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment:** **$2,400,000** per Contract Year (Order Form §3.1). The shortfall payment is 20% of the deficit (Order Form §3.3).
- **Liability cap:** fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months by Customer to Supplier, measured from the event giving rise to the claim (MSA §11.2). If Harrowgate buys only the minimum, the cap is roughly $2.4 million.
- **Payment:** 45 days after receipt of an undisputed invoice (MSA §4.2).
- **Governing law and forum:** Delaware law, with exclusive jurisdiction in New Castle County courts (MSA §§17.1–17.2).

---

## III. Issues, Ranked by Significance

### Issue 1: Change of Control of Customer requires Tessaline's prior written consent **[IMMEDIATE ATTENTION]**

**Where:**
- MSA §15.3 (Change of Control of Customer).
- MSA §1.1(c) (definition of "Change of Control").
- MSA §15.2 (Customer's assignment restriction).
- MSA §15.4 (void transfers).
- Order Form §2.1, which expressly preserves termination "under ... Section 15.3 of the Master Supply Agreement."

**What it says.** Section 15.3 provides:

> "Any Change of Control of Customer, including by merger in which Customer is the surviving entity, shall be deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Customer requiring the prior written consent of Supplier under Section 15.2."

If a Change of Control occurs without that consent, Tessaline may terminate on 30 days' written notice. It has 180 days after it learns of the Change of Control to do so. On termination, "the unpaid balance of the minimum annual purchase commitment under the Order Form for the remainder of the then-current term shall become immediately due and payable by Customer."

**Why the Corvane deal triggers it.** Under the LOI, Harrowgate would be acquired by reverse triangular merger and would survive as a Corvane subsidiary. That structure falls within the Change of Control definition in two ways:

- **§1.1(c)(i):** Corvane would acquire beneficial ownership of more than 50% of Harrowgate's voting equity.
- **§1.1(c)(ii):** it is a merger "whether or not that Party is the surviving entity," after which Harrowgate's pre-closing holders own less than 50%.

Section 15.3 also expressly names a merger in which Customer survives. As a general matter, Delaware courts have not treated a reverse triangular merger as an assignment by operation of law. That default does not help here, because the parties have contracted around it in express terms. No consent has been requested or obtained.

**Why it matters to Harrowgate as customer.**
- Tessaline gains a unilateral exit right, open for 180 days after it learns of the deal. That puts at risk supply of qualified food-contact film.
- Requalifying a replacement supplier would take time. The Quality Agreement's change-control and qualification process in §7 shows how much work is involved in qualifying film.

**Why it matters to Harrowgate as target.**
- **Acceleration exposure.** The acceleration amount is the unpaid balance of the minimum commitment "for the remainder of the then-current term." If closing occurred in early 2027, roughly two years of the Initial Term would remain. The exposure could then approach **$4.8 million or more**, depending on how much has been purchased and how "unpaid balance" is read. This is far larger than the 20% Shortfall Payment in Order Form §3.3, which the parties themselves describe as "a reasonable estimate of Supplier's lost margin."
- **Possible defense.** Harrowgate might argue that full acceleration is an unenforceable penalty, given the parties' own lost-margin estimate in §3.3. We should not rely on that argument in deal planning.
- **Impact on the deal.** Corvane will treat this as a material contract consent. It will likely appear in the disclosure schedules and the closing conditions. An unaddressed consent could delay closing or support a price adjustment or special indemnity demand.
- **Leverage shifts to Tessaline.** Once Tessaline knows Harrowgate needs its consent, it may try to reopen pricing or volume terms. We should plan our approach accordingly.

**Recommended fix and negotiation position.**

1. **Obtain a written consent and waiver from Tessaline before signing the merger agreement.** If that is not possible, the consent should be a closing condition and a listed closing deliverable, with a covenant requiring Harrowgate to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain it. Proposed consent language:

   > "Supplier hereby irrevocably consents, for all purposes of Sections 15.2 and 15.3 of the Master Supply Agreement, to the merger of [Merger Sub] with and into Customer, with Customer surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Corvane Equity Partners IV, L.P. or its affiliate, and to any resulting Change of Control of Customer (the 'Transaction'). Supplier waives any right to terminate the Master Supply Agreement or any Order Form, or to accelerate any amount under Section 15.3, as a result of the Transaction. The Master Supply Agreement and Order Form No. 1 shall remain in full force and effect following the Transaction without modification except as set forth in [the Amendment]."

2. **Amend §15.3 for the future.**
   - Carve out transfers to Affiliates and to private-equity sponsors and their portfolio companies.
   - Limit Tessaline's remedy to termination on reasonable notice, at least 180 days, without acceleration.
   - At minimum, cap any payment at the Shortfall Payment methodology in Order Form §3.3.

   Proposed language:

   > "A Change of Control of Customer shall not constitute an assignment and shall not require Supplier's consent, except that if the acquirer is a direct competitor of Supplier in the manufacture of flexible packaging film, Supplier may terminate this Agreement on one hundred eighty (180) days' written notice given within ninety (90) days after written notice of the Change of Control. No amount shall be accelerated upon any such termination."

3. **Manage timing and confidentiality.**
   - Coordinate with Corvane before contacting Tessaline. Any confidentiality obligations under the LOI may restrict disclosure.
   - MSA §13.1 lets Harrowgate share Tessaline's information with its advisors and financing sources. It does not authorize disclosure of the deal to Tessaline. Any approach to Tessaline should be made under an NDA or clean-team arrangement.

---

### Issue 2: Harrowgate's indemnity is uncapped; Tessaline's is capped

**Where:**
- MSA §11.4 (Customer Indemnity carve-out).
- MSA §10.2 (indemnity by Customer).
- MSA §10.1 (indemnity by Supplier).
- MSA §11.1 (consequential damages exclusion).
- MSA §11.2 (cap).
- MSA §11.3 (mutual exceptions).

**What it says.** Section 11.4 provides:

> "Notwithstanding Section 11.2 or Section 11.1, Customer's obligations under Section 10.2 shall not be subject to any limitation of liability or exclusion of damages set out in this Agreement."

Harrowgate's §10.2 indemnity covers:
- (a) infringement claims relating to Artwork and Customer Materials;
- (b) labeling content, including allergen and nutritional statements;
- (c) "the contents of any Filled Product, including any product liability, personal injury, illness or recall claim," except to the extent caused by nonconforming film;
- (d) Customer's negligence.

Tessaline's reciprocal indemnity in §10.1 has no equivalent carve-out. It covers product defects, infringement and Supplier negligence. It therefore remains subject to the §11.2 cap of fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months, and to the §11.1 waiver of consequential damages. The §11.3 exceptions for fraud, gross negligence, willful misconduct, confidentiality and payment apply equally to both parties and do not fix this imbalance.

**Why it matters to Harrowgate as customer.**
- Harrowgate faces unlimited exposure, including for consequential damages, lost profits and punitive-type amounts paid in third-party settlements. The highest-risk categories for a food producer are allergen-labeling and food-safety recall claims.
- Tessaline's liability for defective film is capped at roughly one year of fees, about $2.4 million at the minimum purchase level. That cap is **below** the $5 million CGL insurance Tessaline must carry under §12.1. In effect, Tessaline's indemnity does not reach its own insurance tower.
- In a contamination event where cause is disputed, for example film migration versus filled-product contents, Harrowgate bears uncapped risk while Tessaline's contribution is limited.

**Why it matters to Harrowgate as target.**
- Corvane's diligence team will flag uncapped indemnity obligations as contingent liabilities.
- The issue may affect valuation, R&W insurance underwriting, which may exclude known uncapped exposures, or special indemnity requests in the merger agreement.
- After closing, the exposure stays with the portfolio company.

**Recommended fix and negotiation position.**

- **Preferred position:** delete §11.4. Both parties' indemnities would then sit under the general cap, subject to the existing mutual §11.3 exceptions.
- **Fallback position:** a **mutual super-cap** for both parties' §10 indemnities. Proposed replacement for §11.4:

  > "11.4 **Indemnity Super-Cap.** Notwithstanding Section 11.2, each Party's aggregate liability for its indemnification obligations under Section 10.1 or Section 10.2, as applicable, shall not exceed the greater of (a) [three (3)] times the fees paid or payable by Customer to Supplier under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, and (b) [$5,000,000]. Section 11.1 shall not limit amounts payable to a third party under a Third-Party Claim for which a Party is obligated to indemnify under Section 10."

- **Supporting argument:** tie the super-cap to the insurance limits both parties already carry under §12.1, namely $5 million CGL and $2 million recall. Neither party then takes on uninsured risk.

---

### Issue 3: Automatic five-year renewals with a narrow opt-out window

**Where:**
- Order Form §2.2 (Renewal).
- Order Form §2.1 (Initial Term).
- Order Form §3.1 (Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment).
- MSA §2.1, which ties the MSA's term to the Order Form.

**What it says.**
- After the three-year Initial Term, the MSA and Order Form "shall automatically renew for successive five (5) year Renewal Terms."
- A notice of non-renewal "is effective only if it is delivered ... no earlier than sixty (60) days and no later than thirty (30) days before the end of the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Term." A notice delivered outside that period "is of no effect."
- All Order Form terms, including the **$2,400,000** minimum annual purchase commitment, carry into each Renewal Term.
- The Order Form controls over the MSA under MSA §1.3.

**Why it matters to Harrowgate as customer.**
- Missing the window by a single day locks Harrowgate into five more years. That means at least $12 million in minimum purchases, with shortfall exposure under §3.3.
- Notice sent too early is also void.
- The pricing mechanism in §4.3, a resin-index adjustment, also rolls forward. Harrowgate would get no chance to re-tender or re-price.
- **First window:** the Initial Term runs three years from March 1, 2026. The first window therefore falls approximately between **December 31, 2028 and January 30, 2029**. Please confirm the end-of-term date convention before docketing.

**Why it matters to Harrowgate as target.**
- Corvane will inherit a long-tail volume commitment that could outlast its likely holding period.
- Combined with Issue 1, a renewal could also enlarge the acceleration base. Section 15.3 accelerates the commitment "for the remainder of the then-current term," so a Change of Control in an early Renewal Term could expose up to five years of minimums.

**Recommended fix and negotiation position.**

- Replace the renewal language in §2.2 with the following:

  > "2.2 **Renewal.** At the end of the Initial Term, this Order Form and the Master Supply Agreement shall renew for successive one (1) year Renewal Terms unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal at least one hundred eighty (180) days before the end of the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Term."

- **Alternative:** mutual opt-in renewal, under which the agreement renews only by signed written agreement.
- **Additional ask:** Supplier must send a written reminder 60 days before the window opens.
- **In any case:** docket the first non-renewal window now in Harrowgate's contract-management system. After closing, transition the reminder to Corvane's portfolio-company counsel.

---

### Issue 4: Tessaline may assign freely; Harrowgate may not

**Where:**
- MSA §15.1 (Assignment by Supplier).
- Compare MSA §15.2 (Assignment by Customer).

**What it says.**
- "Supplier may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the consent of Customer, to any person, and may delegate any of its obligations ... to any Affiliate or subcontractor." Supplier need only notify Customer within 30 days *after* the assignment.
- By contrast, §15.2 bars Harrowgate from any assignment, "whether voluntarily, by operation of law or otherwise," without Tessaline's consent.
- Delaware generally treats contract rights as freely assignable unless the contract restricts assignment. Section 15.1 removes any restriction on Tessaline.

**Why it matters to Harrowgate as customer.**
- The agreement, and with it Harrowgate's pricing, forecasts, Specifications and Artwork, could pass to:
  - a supplier that has not passed Harrowgate's qualification process;
  - a financially weaker entity;
  - a supplier affiliated with a Harrowgate competitor.
- Harrowgate would remain bound by the $2.4 million annual minimum to whoever holds the contract.
- A partial assignment could split supply of the four Part Nos. across different counterparties.
- The change-control protections in MSA §6.3 and Quality Agreement §7 cover changes in manufacturing site and materials. Arguably they do not cover a change in the identity of the contracting supplier.

**Why it matters to Harrowgate as target.**
- Corvane will want assurance that a key input supply contract cannot be transferred to an unknown or competing counterparty.
- The one-sided clause also highlights the broader imbalance in the assignment provisions. Corvane may ask that it be fixed in the same amendment.

**Recommended fix and negotiation position.** Make the provision mutual. Proposed replacement for §§15.1–15.2:

> "15.1 **Assignment.** Neither Party may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the prior written consent of the other Party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Either Party may, without consent but on prior written notice, assign this Agreement in its entirety to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of the business to which this Agreement relates, provided that (a) the assignee assumes this Agreement in writing, and (b) in the case of assignment by Supplier, the assignee is not a competitor of Customer or an Affiliate of a competitor of Customer, and the Products continue to be manufactured at sites qualified under the Quality Agreement. Supplier may subcontract manufacturing only in compliance with Section 6.3."

---

## IV. Quality Agreement: No Issues Identified

I reviewed the Quality Agreement carefully, because it interacts with MSA §§6–7 and the warranty remedies. I recommend **no renegotiation**. Its terms are customary or favorable to Harrowgate:

- **18-month warranty period** after delivery (§5.1). This is reasonable for packaging film. It expressly covers Latent Defects (§5.2).
- **10-business-day rejection window** (§6.2). This is customary. Acceptance is "for purposes of incoming inspection only" and does not cut off warranty or Latent Defect rights.
- **Remedies at Customer's election** (§5.4), with replacement or credit at Supplier's cost. These are expressly in addition to the MSA §10.1 indemnity.
- **Strong supplier obligations:**
  - GFSI-benchmarked certification (§4.1);
  - release testing and CoAs (§§4.3–4.4);
  - 90-day change notice and approval (§7);
  - 24-hour quality-event notice and recall cooperation (§8);
  - four-hour traceability (§8.3).
- **Recall decisions** rest with Harrowgate (§8.2). Recall costs are left to the MSA, which is why fixing Issue 2 matters.

The Quality Agreement ranks last in the §1.3 order of precedence, so it cannot override the Order Form or MSA terms discussed above.

---

## V. Recommended Next Steps

1. **Now, before signing:**
   - Brief Corvane's counsel on MSA §15.3 and the acceleration exposure.
   - Agree a joint approach and a confidentiality arrangement for contacting Tessaline.
   - Make sure the merger agreement lists the Tessaline consent and waiver as a required consent and closing deliverable.
2. **Single approach to Tessaline:** request the consent and waiver (Issue 1) together with an amendment addressing:
   - §11.4 (Issue 2);
   - Order Form §2.2 (Issue 3);
   - §15.1 (Issue 4).

   Keeping it to one negotiation limits the number of times Tessaline can extract concessions.
3. **Docket** the first Order Form §2.2 non-renewal window, approximately December 31, 2028 to January 30, 2029, subject to confirmation.
4. **Quantify** current-year purchases against the $2.4 million minimum, so we can model the §15.3 acceleration exposure and any §3.3 shortfall.

---

## VI. Questions Before Finalizing

1. **Timing.** What is the target signing date, and what is the expected gap between signing and closing? Is Corvane willing to sign before the consent is in hand, with the consent as a closing condition?
2. **Disclosure.** Does the LOI restrict disclosing the transaction to counterparties? Who should approach Tessaline: Harrowgate management or counsel?
3. **Structure.** Is the merger still a reverse triangular merger with Harrowgate surviving? Is any pre-closing restructuring planned, such as an asset drop-down, that would separately implicate §15.2?
4. **Commercial priorities.**
   - How dependent is Harrowgate on Tessaline, and are qualified alternative suppliers available?
   - Would Harrowgate accept a modest pricing or volume concession to secure the consent and amendments?
   - Does Corvane intend to keep Tessaline as a supplier after closing, or consolidate supply across its portfolio?
5. **Execution status.** The copies in the folder show blank signature blocks. Please confirm that fully executed versions exist and that there have been no amendments or later Order Forms.

Please let me know your views on these points, and I will finalize the memo and prepare the draft consent and amendment.

**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** October 18, 2026
**Re:** Harrowgate Provisions, Inc.: Review of Tessaline Polymers Supply Documents in Connection with the Proposed Corvane Acquisition

**Privileged & Confidential | Attorney Work Product**

---

## I. Summary

I reviewed three documents together:

* the Master Supply Agreement dated March 1, 2026 (the "**MSA**");
* Order Form No. 1 of the same date (the "**Order Form**"); and
* the Quality Agreement of the same date (the "**QA**").

All three are between Tessaline Polymers LLC ("**Tessaline**" or "**Supplier**") and Harrowgate Provisions, Inc. ("**Harrowgate**" or "**Customer**"). They are governed by Delaware law (MSA § 17.1).

Under MSA § 1.3, conflicts are resolved in this order: Order Form, then MSA, then QA.

**Key commercial terms:**

| Term | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Initial Term | Three years from the March 1, 2026 Effective Date, running to approximately March 1, 2029 | Order Form § 2.1 |
| Minimum annual purchase commitment | **$2,400,000** per Contract Year | Order Form § 3.1 |
| Shortfall payment | 20% of any shortfall | Order Form § 3.3 |
| Liability cap | Fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months | MSA § 11.2 |
| Payment terms | 45 days after receipt of undisputed invoice | MSA § 4.2 |

I identified **three issues** that warrant action. They are ranked below by significance. **Issue 1 (change-of-control consent) needs immediate attention before Harrowgate signs a definitive merger agreement with Corvane.**

I found no issues in the Quality Agreement that require renegotiation (see Part III).

### Ranked Issues at a Glance

| Rank | Issue | Location | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Change of Control of Customer requires Tessaline's consent; triggers termination and acceleration | MSA § 15.3 (with §§ 1.1(c), 15.2, 15.4) | **IMMEDIATE: before signing** |
| 2 | Automatic five-year renewals with a narrow 60-to-30-day opt-out window, carrying the $2.4M annual minimum | Order Form § 2.2 (with §§ 2.1, 3.1, 3.3) | High: renegotiate alongside Issue 1; docket now |
| 3 | Tessaline may assign freely without consent; one-sided against Harrowgate | MSA § 15.1 (compare § 15.2) | Moderate: raise in the same consent negotiation |

---

## II. Issues

### Issue 1: Change-of-Control Consent Triggered by the Corvane Merger (IMMEDIATE ATTENTION)

**Location:**
* MSA § 15.3 (Change of Control of Customer)
* MSA § 1.1(c) (definition of "Change of Control")
* MSA § 15.2 (Customer assignment restriction)
* MSA § 15.4 (void transfers)
* Order Form § 2.1, which cross-references termination under MSA § 15.3

**What the documents say.** Section 15.3 provides that "[a]ny Change of Control of Customer, including by merger in which Customer is the surviving entity, shall be deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Customer requiring the prior written consent of Supplier under Section 15.2."

If a Change of Control occurs without that consent, Tessaline may terminate on 30 days' written notice at any time within 180 days after it learns of the Change of Control. On termination, "the unpaid balance of the minimum annual purchase commitment under the Order Form for the remainder of the then-current term shall become immediately due and payable."

"Change of Control" in § 1.1(c) is broad. It covers:
* acquisition of more than 50% of the voting equity of a Party; and
* any merger, "whether or not that Party is the surviving entity," after which the pre-transaction holders hold less than 50% of the surviving entity or its ultimate parent.

**Why it matters.**

* **The Corvane deal triggers the clause.** A reverse triangular merger with Corvane will result in Corvane owning all of Harrowgate's voting equity. That falls squarely within both prongs (i) and (ii) of the definition. It is also expressly captured by § 15.3's reference to a merger in which Customer survives.
  * As a general matter, Delaware courts have not treated a reverse triangular merger as an assignment by the surviving target by operation of law.
  * That default does not help here. The parties have contracted around it by deeming a Change of Control to be an assignment.
  * No consent has been requested or obtained.

* **Exposure as Tessaline's customer.** Tessaline would hold a unilateral option, for 180 days after learning of the closing, to:
  * terminate a supply relationship for food-grade film that Harrowgate presumably depends on; and
  * accelerate the unpaid minimum commitment.

  Measured from a closing in the near term, the remainder of the Initial Term runs to roughly March 1, 2029. On a natural reading, acceleration could reach the unpaid portion of the $2,400,000 annual minimum for each remaining Contract Year. That is potentially well over $5 million, payable immediately, while Harrowgate simultaneously loses its supply.

  The clause is ambiguous on whether "for the remainder of the then-current term" captures only the current Contract Year or all remaining Contract Years. We should assume Tessaline will argue for the latter.

* **Additional risk under § 15.4.** Section 15.4 states that any assignment "in violation of this Section 15 is void." Because a Change of Control is "deemed an assignment," Tessaline could argue that the agreement does not validly continue for the benefit of the post-closing company. That would add uncertainty even if Tessaline does not formally terminate.

* **Exposure as an acquisition target.**
  * Corvane will treat this as a material contract with a consent requirement. It will need to appear on the disclosure schedules against the no-conflicts and material-contracts representations.
  * An unaddressed acceleration right is a quantifiable contingent liability. Corvane may seek to price it through a purchase-price reduction, special indemnity or escrow.
  * Tessaline also gains significant leverage once it knows of the deal. It could use the consent request to extract pricing or term concessions.
  * MSA § 13.1 permits disclosure of Confidential Information to advisors and financing sources. Harrowgate should still manage the timing and content of its approach to Tessaline carefully, consistent with any confidentiality obligations under the LOI.

**Recommended fix / negotiation position.**

1. **Obtain a written consent and waiver from Tessaline before signing the merger agreement, or at minimum before closing.** Proposed language:

   > "Tessaline Polymers LLC hereby irrevocably consents, for all purposes of Sections 15.2 and 15.3 of the Master Supply Agreement dated as of March 1, 2026 (the 'Agreement'), to the Change of Control of Harrowgate Provisions, Inc. resulting from the merger contemplated by the Agreement and Plan of Merger among Harrowgate Provisions, Inc., Corvane Equity Partners IV, L.P. (or its affiliates) and the other parties thereto, and to any related change in the direct or indirect ownership of Harrowgate Provisions, Inc. Supplier waives any right to terminate the Agreement, accelerate any amount under Section 15.3, or treat the Agreement as void or assigned under Section 15.4, in each case arising from such transaction. The Agreement shall continue in full force and effect following the consummation of such transaction."

2. **Merger agreement mechanics.** List the Tessaline consent as a required third-party consent in the disclosure schedules. Depending on how important the relationship is, list it either as:
   * a closing deliverable or condition; or
   * a covenant to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain it, with a negotiated allocation of risk if it is not obtained.

   Resist any obligation to pay Tessaline a consent fee without client approval.

3. **Longer-term fix (if Tessaline will reopen the MSA).** Amend § 15.3 so that it:
   * applies only to a Change of Control in which Customer's business is acquired by a direct competitor of Supplier; and
   * replaces termination plus acceleration with a termination right that carries no acceleration of future minimums.

   At minimum, delete the acceleration sentence and the "including by merger in which Customer is the surviving entity" language.

---

### Issue 2: Automatic Five-Year Renewals with a Narrow Opt-Out Window

**Location:** Order Form § 2.2 (Renewal), read with Order Form §§ 2.1, 3.1 and 3.3 and MSA § 2.1.

**What the documents say.** At the end of the three-year Initial Term, the MSA and Order Form "shall automatically renew for successive five (5) year Renewal Terms."

Non-renewal notice is effective only if delivered under MSA § 16 "no earlier than sixty (60) days and no later than thirty (30) days before the end of the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Term." Notice outside that window "is of no effect."

All Order Form terms carry into each Renewal Term, expressly including the $2,400,000 Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment (§ 3.1) and the pricing mechanism. Because the Order Form governs over the MSA under MSA § 1.3, these renewal terms control.

**Why it matters.**

* **As Tessaline's customer.**
  * A missed 30-day window locks Harrowgate into five more years of minimum purchases. That is a commitment of at least $12,000,000 over the Renewal Term.
  * Any shortfall is backed by the 20% Shortfall Payment in Order Form § 3.3.
  * The renewal is also disproportionate. The Renewal Term is longer than the Initial Term.
  * The opt-out window is unusually narrow. A notice sent too early is as ineffective as one sent too late.
  * For the Initial Term ending around March 1, 2029, the window falls roughly in early-to-late January 2029. We should confirm the exact dates by counting calendar days under MSA § 1.2.

* **As an acquisition target.**
  * Corvane will inherit the commitment. The renewal also interacts with Issue 1: under § 15.3, acceleration reaches the minimum "for the remainder of the then-current term." If a Change of Control occurs during a five-year Renewal Term, the accelerated amount could be far larger.
  * Through ownership transitions, notice addresses (MSA § 16.1 names Harrowgate's Chief Legal Officer) and personnel may change. That raises the risk that the window will be missed.
  * Corvane's diligence team will likely flag long-tail volume commitments as a constraint on post-closing procurement consolidation.

**Recommended fix / negotiation position.**

1. **Proposed revised Order Form § 2.2:**

   > "2.2 **Renewal.** At the end of the Initial Term, the Master Supply Agreement and this Order Form shall automatically renew for successive one (1) year Renewal Terms unless either Party gives the other Party written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days before the end of the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Term. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith any adjustment to the Minimum Annual Purchase Commitment for each Renewal Term no later than one hundred twenty (120) days before its commencement."

   An alternative is to replace automatic renewal with renewal only by mutual written agreement (opt-in).

2. **Remove the "no earlier than" limitation.** A non-renewal notice should be effective whenever delivered before the deadline.

3. **Docket immediately.** Calendar the Initial Term non-renewal window now, with reminders well in advance. Include the deadline in the transition checklist delivered to Corvane.

4. **Bundle with Issue 1.** Raise this amendment in the same conversation as the change-of-control consent. Tessaline may resist, but the consent request is the natural moment to reopen commercial terms.

---

### Issue 3: Tessaline May Assign the Agreement Freely; One-Sided Assignment Clause

**Location:** MSA § 15.1 (Assignment by Supplier), compared with MSA § 15.2 (Assignment by Customer).

**What the documents say.** Section 15.1 provides that "Supplier may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the consent of Customer, to any person." Tessaline may also delegate obligations to any Affiliate or subcontractor. The only protection is notice within 30 days *after* the assignment.

By contrast, § 15.2 bars Harrowgate from assigning "voluntarily, by operation of law or otherwise" without Tessaline's prior written consent. Section 15.3 extends that restriction to Harrowgate's own change of control.

**Why it matters.**

* **As Tessaline's customer.**
  * Delaware generally treats contract rights as freely assignable unless the contract restricts assignment. Here, the contract expressly confirms Tessaline's freedom.
  * Tessaline could transfer Harrowgate's supply agreement, together with its pricing, forecasts and Confidential Information, to:
    * a competitor of Harrowgate or a competitor's affiliate; or
    * a supplier that has not passed, or has failed, Harrowgate's food-safety qualification.
  * Harrowgate would remain bound to purchase the $2,400,000 annual minimum from that assignee.
  * The QA change-control protections in QA § 7.1 and MSA § 6.3 address changes in manufacturing site and materials. They do not clearly prevent a wholesale change in the counterparty.
  * Partial assignment could split the supply across entities. That would complicate quality accountability.
  * Recourse against an assignee would remain subject to the MSA § 11.2 cap of 12 months' fees.

* **As an acquisition target.**
  * The asymmetry is conspicuous. Harrowgate's own change of control triggers consent and acceleration, while Tessaline can be sold or can assign the contract at will.
  * Corvane is buying Harrowgate partly for the stability of its supply chain. It will view an unrestricted counterparty assignment right as a diligence concern.

**Recommended fix / negotiation position.** Make the clause mutual. Proposed revised § 15.1:

> "15.1 **Assignment.** Neither Party may assign, delegate or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations under it, whether voluntarily, by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other Party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed; provided that either Party may assign this Agreement in its entirety, without consent but on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, to a successor to all or substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates that (a) is not a competitor of the other Party, (b) assumes this Agreement in writing, and (c) in the case of an assignment by Supplier, maintains the certifications required by Section 4.1 of the Quality Agreement and manufactures the Products at a site approved under Section 6.3. Supplier may delegate obligations to subcontractors only with Customer's prior written approval and shall remain responsible for their performance."

Conforming changes would be made to §§ 15.2 and 15.3. This fix pairs naturally with the narrowed change-of-control clause proposed under Issue 1.

## III. Quality Agreement: No Issues Requiring Renegotiation

I reviewed the QA in full, including how it interacts with MSA §§ 6, 7 and 10. Its terms are customer-favorable or market-standard, and I do not recommend reopening it:

* **Warranty and remedies.**
  * The 18-month warranty period after delivery (QA § 5.1) is reasonable for packaging film.
  * Remedies at Customer's election are replacement or credit, with Supplier bearing return freight (QA § 5.4).
  * These remedies are expressly in addition to MSA § 10.1 indemnity rights.
* **Rejection window.** The 10-business-day window (QA § 6.2) is adequate. Acceptance is "for purposes of incoming inspection only" and preserves rights for Latent Defects and nonconformities discovered during the warranty period.
* **Change control and quality systems.**
  * QA § 7 has 90-day notice and approval requirements.
  * QA § 4.1 requires GFSI-benchmarked certification.
  * QA § 8.1 imposes 24-hour notification duties.
  * QA § 8.2 gives Customer sole recall authority.
  * QA § 8.3 has robust traceability requirements.
* **Precedence.** The QA sits last in the § 1.3 order of precedence. I found no conflict with the Order Form or MSA that would undercut its protections.
